key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically extract key longitudinal breast cancer variables from dense clinical notes with high agreement to expert abstraction.
clinical_relevance: This approach could reduce the manual chart-review burden in oncology research and help scale retrospective data extraction from narrative medical records.
method: Open-source pipeline used general-purpose LLMs without fine-tuning or hand-selected documents
Tested on 100 randomly selected patients from a complex breast cancer cohort in a HIPAA-compliant setting
Compared model outputs with oncologist abstraction, genetic testing records, and some coordinator abstraction
evidence_signal: Across GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, the pipeline reached 90%-100% concordance for several key variables, and in a separate 97-patient cohort it showed similar recurrence detection performance.
watch_item: Performance was weaker for therapy-line reconstruction, and results still need replication and validation across other institutions and diseases.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
